subject: Invoice submission options: XML vs CSV + portal-first / email fallback (sandbox test plan)

Subject: Invoice submission format and daily batch question

Hi Tessa,

Quick intro — Daniel here from Frostline Analytics. We're getting our billing flows aligned for Redwood and I have a couple of questions before we send a first batch.

High level: we plan to send a daily batched file with multiple invoices (each invoice may reference one or multiple POs). Current internal systems export either CSV or a small XML payload. Which format would you prefer for the ingestion pipeline (XML with nested line items vs a flat CSV)? Are there specific required fields we should include to maximize PO-match success?

I've attached a draft CSV export from our ERP to show typical columns and examples.

Notes / asks:
- Is portal upload required, or can we email batches to a designated SMTP endpoint as a fallback?
- If email fallback is allowed, do you require a subject token or a specific ack header?
- Character set / encoding requirements (UTF-8 OK?)
- Any example XML skeleton you prefer for nested line items (taxes, discounts, cost centers)?

Attached: draft_invoice_sample.csv (small, 28KB)

Appreciate any guidance. We can stand up a sandbox/test file this week.

Thanks,
Daniel Ruiz
Senior Operations Manager
Frostline Analytics

Subject: Re: Invoice submission format and daily batch question

Hi Daniel — thanks for the sample and the clear list of questions. Looping in Kimberly (billing ingestion) and Vanessa (vendor onboarding) so we can give a concise ingestion plan + onboarding checklist.

Short answer up front: portal-first for onboarding and day-to-day, with email (SMTP) as a supported fallback for legacy systems. We do accept both CSV and XML — portal uploads prefer a canonical CSV, email fallback supports either CSV or a specific XML schema (see Kimberly's note below). UTF-8 is required.

For the onboarding flow we'll need:
- Completed vendor onboarding form (attached) with legal entity / remit-to / tax IDs
- Sample invoice files (one small CSV and one small XML) for compatibility testing
- Point of contact for test coordination and an expected send cadence

Operational guidance / next steps:
1) Please complete the attached vendor_onboarding_form.pdf and return to vendor-ops@redwood.com.
2) Kimberly will provide the field mapping and an example XML skeleton you can use for the test run.
3) We'll provision a sandbox mailbox and an SFTP endpoint for larger payloads; you can run a single test and we'll validate PO matching.

Vanessa — can you confirm the onboarding form fields we still want optional vs mandatory (we'd like to avoid blocking by requiring remittance contact if the entity is already verified).

Thanks — if you can do the onboarding form + two sample files by Thursday we can schedule a test Friday.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Program Manager, Vendor Ops
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Invoice submission format and daily batch question — field mapping + sample XML/CSV

Hi Daniel — following up with the specifics for ingestion and PO-matching. I'm including a minimal XML example and notes for the CSV to help your export team.

Kafka-sized TL;DR: portal CSV preferred (canonical header order below). Email fallback supports a namespaced XML (we validate by XSD) or CSV. Always UTF-8. Use ISO-8601 date fields.

Required invoice-level fields (CSV column names we expect):
- invoice_number
- invoice_date (YYYY-MM-DD)
- remit_entity_code (internal code if you have multiple remit entities)
- bill_to_entity_code
- total_amount (decimal, two places)
- currency (ISO 4217)
- PO_number (if present)
- vendor_tax_id
- contact_email (for ack)

Line-item fields (if flattened CSV with multiple rows per invoice):
- invoice_number
- line_number
- PO_number
- item_description
- quantity
- unit_price
- line_net_amount
- tax_amount
- cost_center_code (optional)
- discount_amount (optional)

CSV tips: send one row per line item; repeat invoice-level fields on each line. For single-line invoices a single row is fine. File name convention (for email fallback) we recommend: FI-<vendorid>-YYYYMMDD-<sequence>.csv and include PO token in subject: "PO:<PO_NUMBER>" to help auto-route.

Email fallback requirements:
- Subject must include vendor shortcode or PO token (e.g., "PO:123456" or "VENDOR:FRSTLINE").
- Raw email body should not inline attachments as images; attach files as proper MIME attachments.
- Ack header: we return X-Redwood-Invoice-Ack: <ACK_TOKEN> in our confirmation email; include the contact_email column so we can push ack to correct address.

XML skeleton (minimal):
-----BEGIN XML EXAMPLE-----
<Invoices xmlns="http://redwood.example.com/invoice/1.0">
  <Invoice>
    <InvoiceNumber>FR-2026-0001</InvoiceNumber>
    <InvoiceDate>2026-12-18</InvoiceDate>
    <Currency>USD</Currency>
    <TotalAmount>1200.00</TotalAmount>
    <VendorTaxId>12-3456789</VendorTaxId>
    <LineItems>
      <Line>
        <LineNumber>1</LineNumber>
        <PONumber>PO-54321</PONumber>
        <Description>Consulting hours</Description>
        <Quantity>10</Quantity>
        <UnitPrice>100.00</UnitPrice>
        <LineNetAmount>1000.00</LineNetAmount>
        <TaxAmount>200.00</TaxAmount>
      </Line>
    </LineItems>
  </Invoice>
</Invoices>
-----END XML EXAMPLE-----

Namespace/XSD: we'll provide an XSD for validation; please avoid custom namespaces unless pre-agreed.

PO matching rules (summary):
- Exact PO_number match preferred; we also accept short-PONumber if you include entity code.
- If multiple invoices reference a single PO, we'll accumulate against the same PO until it's closed.
- If PO is missing, invoices will be routed to exceptions and require manual intervention (longer SLA).

Attachments: I've attached a canonical invoice_template_v2.csv with header order we expect.

Happy to hop on a short 15-min call to run through one live test. If you send a sample to the sandbox mailbox we'll validate and push an ack.

Kimberly Park
Billing & Ingestion Lead
Redwood Inference
